Heard learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner and learned Additional Standing Counsel appearing for the State- Opposite Party.
Perused the materials placed before this Court.

3. The present bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the Petitioner for regular bail in connection with C.T. Case No.913 of 1974, arising out of Bhawanipatna Town P.S.Case No.311 of 2021, pending in the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Bhawanipatna for alleged commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 342, 376(3), 276(2)(n), 506 of the Indian Penal Code read with section 6 of POCSO Act.
4. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that earlier this matter was not before any other Bench of this Court.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Petitioner is languishing in custody since 21.07.2024.
Further he contended that in the meantime the investigation has progressed substantially and final charge sheet is likely to be filed very soon.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner also submitted that the Petitioner as well as the victim were in love relationship.

1 married and thereafter the Petitioner was arrested and languishing in custody since the date of his arrest i.e. on 21.07.2024.

On perusal of the order sheet, it appears that pursuant to the notice issued by this Court the informant appeared through virtual mode on 10.09.2024, reveals that this Court recorded the statement of the victim to the effect that the victim stated that she is aged about 22 years and at the moment she is staying with her in-laws and she has been blessed with a male child.
Further the victim expressed that she does not want to oppose the release of the Petitioner on bail.

5. . Learned counsel appearing for the informant on the other hand on instruction submitted that the victim has already married to the Petitioner and they were living peacefully as husband and wife and blessed with a child in the meantime.
On such ground learned counsel for the informant is not interested in opposing the bail application of the present Petitioner.
6. Learned Additional Standing Counsel on the other hand objected to the release of the Petitioner on bail on the ground that the investigation is still on.
He further contended that the allegations made in the F.I.R. are serious in nature.
On such ground, learned counsel for the State submitted that the Petitioner shall not be enlarged on bail.

7. Having heard learned counsel for the respective parties, on a careful examination of the materials on record, further taking note of the fact that the victim, who is 23 years of age married the Petitioner and both are living as husband and wife and they were blessed with a child, this Court in the larger interest of justice, is inclined to release the Petitioner on bail subject to such terms and conditions that would be imposed by the learned court in seisin over the matter.

7. Hence, it is directed that the Petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing bail bond of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court in seisin over the matter.
Violation of any other conditions shall entail cancellation of the bail application.
8. The BLAPL is, accordingly, disposed of.
( A.K. Mohapatra) Judge RKS Location: High Court of Orissa Rajesh Kumar Naik vs State Of Odisha .....
